description: SB1-oriented rule catalog. Transferred VC5 rules are hypotheses until validated with Speedy Blupi evidence. No runtime dependency on blood2_recon.

rules.title: A repeated field read may mean the source had no cached local
rules.symptom: Native reloads a member chain; ours keeps one value live.
rules.construct: Repeated member expression versus one named pointer/value local.
rules.explanation: VC5 may reload across calls or aliasing stores instead of keeping an optimizer-created cache.
rules.experiment: Remove the local and restore the full member expression at each native read.
rules.not_when: Do not do this when native reads once and reuses the value.
rules.keywords: member reload cache alias local

blupi_evidence.outcome: STRICT after replacing explicit scalar caches with repeated coordinate expressions (direct member access); explicit caches prevented matching

rules.title: A value read once may have had a named local
rules.symptom: Native loads a value once and reuses its register; ours reloads it.
rules.construct: One local holding a field, call result, list head, or repeated size.
rules.explanation: A local forces one evaluation where an intervening call/store may alias.
rules.experiment: Introduce one local at the likely original declaration point and reuse it.
rules.not_when: Avoid when VC5 already reuses the cheap expression.
rules.keywords: cached local call result pointer

rules.title: Block scope can reuse dead stack slots
rules.symptom: Stack offsets or frame size differ while the main instruction shape is close.
rules.construct: Place a local inside its use block or at function scope.
rules.explanation: VC5 may assign inner-block locals to slots whose prior values are dead.
rules.experiment: Compare the evidenced scope and declaration lifetime; inspect debug output if available.
rules.not_when: This does not explain a register-only difference.
rules.keywords: scope stack slot frame local lifetime

rules.title: Local declaration order is usually inert
rules.symptom: Only local slot order or SIB operand order differs.
rules.construct: Swap adjacent local declarations.
rules.explanation: Corpus results show declaration swaps rarely alter optimized code.
rules.experiment: Try one evidence-backed order only after checking TU context.
rules.not_when: Do not permute declarations broadly.
rules.keywords: declaration order stack slots inert

rules.title: Independent statements can preserve native store order
rules.symptom: The same operations appear in a different order.
rules.construct: Order independent assignments as they appear in native.
rules.explanation: VC5 commonly retains source statement order at /O2.
rules.experiment: Reorder one semantics-independent pair and compare the whole TU.
rules.not_when: Check flags and dependencies before reordering.
rules.keywords: store order statement order scheduling

blupi_evidence.outcome: A register-only ECX/EDX residue was NOT moved by top/before count probes 0-64 but was fixed by writing pos.x before pos.y; identical prefix grew 3,381 -> 4,886 bytes.

rules.title: /O1 can move stores that /O2 leaves in source order
rules.symptom: /O1 and /O2 disagree on independent store order.
rules.construct: Keep the source order evidenced by the /O2 target.
rules.explanation: The size-oriented path can schedule independent stores differently.
rules.experiment: Confirm the owning TU flags before changing source.
rules.not_when: Do not apply from a single image without flag evidence.
rules.keywords: O1 O2 store scheduling

rules.title: A call comparison and a local comparison can use different boolean code
rules.symptom: Native uses neg/sbb while ours uses test/setcc, or the reverse.
rules.construct: Compare the call expression directly versus a local holding its result.
rules.explanation: VC5 selects a different boolean idiom from these source forms.
rules.experiment: Compile both forms with the real return type.
rules.not_when: Check byte versus integer return width first.
rules.keywords: boolean call local compare setcc

rules.title: Result width selects byte or dword instructions
rules.symptom: Native uses AL while ours uses EAX, or movsx differs from movzx.
rules.construct: Match the declared return or member width and signedness.
rules.explanation: The prototype and member types control extension and result width.
rules.experiment: Check the shared declaration before changing the caller.
rules.not_when: Do not override a fixed SDK prototype.
rules.keywords: type width signed char return

blupi_evidence.outcome: char-return candidate emitted 32 bytes and mismatched; int __cdecl candidate matched the 34-byte target body in a 48-byte COFF window

rules.title: VC5 folds within an expression but keeps some statement boundaries
rules.symptom: Native performs two constant operations; ours combines them, or vice versa.
rules.construct: Split or merge arithmetic at the evidenced local/statement boundary.
rules.explanation: Expression folding does not necessarily cross a stored local.
rules.experiment: Compile the two minimal source forms at the same function site.
rules.not_when: A genuinely wrong constant is a source difference.
rules.keywords: constant folding statement local

rules.title: Branch layout often follows source block order
rules.symptom: Equivalent blocks appear in another order or conditional polarity.
rules.construct: Restore the native then/else ordering and condition shape.
rules.explanation: VC5 commonly emits the source then-block first.
rules.experiment: Compare one condition/body rearrangement at the same flags.
rules.not_when: Do not invert semantics based only on address layout.
rules.keywords: branch layout condition polarity

blupi_evidence.outcome: zero-dimension test before clamp changed branch layout and produced a strict 108-byte target body

rules.title: Destructor scopes can distinguish fall-through from early return
rules.symptom: Native branches to a destructor test; ours returns to the epilogue.
rules.construct: A scoped fall-through block versus an early return.
rules.explanation: A live destructor joins cleanup paths differently.
rules.experiment: Restore the source scope/exit form supported by object lifetime evidence.
rules.not_when: Trivial locals may not show this effect.
rules.keywords: destructor cleanup early return scope

rules.title: Several guards can differ from one joined exit
rules.symptom: Native has distinct guard exits; ours joins them into one path.
rules.construct: Separate guard returns versus a shared final return.
rules.explanation: VC5 preserves different exit structures when cleanup and branch joins differ.
rules.experiment: Try only the guard structure indicated by native control flow.
rules.not_when: Check destructor scope and conditions first.
rules.keywords: guard returns exit branch

blupi_evidence.outcome: Target-based helicopter guard and creature/player-position skip plus uninitialized IntersectRect output changed a 512-byte baseline candidate to 608 bytes; target body is 538 bytes and remains MISMATCH. A short type local had no further code-size effect; negative only for these tested source forms.

rules.title: Inline decisions can vary by caller site
rules.symptom: The same helper is called at some sites and expanded at others.
rules.construct: Restore the real helper call sites and wrapper layers.
rules.explanation: VC5 spends a caller-local inline budget; expansion size and nesting matter.
rules.experiment: List calls in source order and test one caller with the real helper body.
rules.not_when: Do not add inline/noinline hints to force a call list.
rules.keywords: inline budget call sites wrappers

rules.title: Expanded wrappers can add later inline decisions
rules.symptom: Nested helper calls expand at sites with an unexpected order.
rules.construct: Restore an evidenced wrapper call instead of direct calls.
rules.explanation: Nested sites may be considered after direct sites and in reverse order.
rules.experiment: Compare direct and wrapper forms in one caller.
rules.not_when: The observed order is VC5-specific and bounded.
rules.keywords: nested wrapper inline reverse order

rules.title: Call a real inline member instead of open-coding it
rules.symptom: A helper body is expanded but register or load choices differ.
rules.construct: Use the original helper call expression when its definition is available.
rules.explanation: Inline-body source context can affect the generated sequence.
rules.experiment: Compare one call site against the open-coded body.
rules.not_when: Do not invent a helper absent from source evidence.
rules.keywords: inline member open code helper

rules.title: /O1 can leave larger inline bodies out of line
rules.symptom: Helper calls differ between /O1 and /O2.
rules.construct: Use the actual per-TU optimization level.
rules.explanation: VC5 /O1 and /O2 can choose different inline shapes.
rules.experiment: Compile both authentic flag sets before changing helper source.
rules.not_when: Do not transfer a project-wide flag assumption to every TU.
rules.keywords: O1 O2 inline calls optimization

rules.title: Register-only residues may come from TU-wide compiler context
rules.symptom: Instruction shape is stable but registers or commutative operands differ.
rules.construct: Test authentic TU context before rewriting expressions.
rules.explanation: A TU symbol counter can select among equal-cost code sequences.
rules.experiment: Use count probes at top, end, and before the function on scratch copies.
rules.not_when: A probe is diagnostic only; never keep artificial declarations.
rules.keywords: symbol counter register x87 SIB TU

blupi_evidence.tu: button.cpp; sound.h included before member bodies
blupi_evidence.outcome: SB1 SP3 count probes: top and before:MouseMove restore STRICT at counts 7-14 and 23-30; end probes do not restore through count 32. Pre-function declaration context is measured; exact counter phase is inferred from placement response. SB1 confirmation incl. resolution by genuine declarations: see BLUPI-CTX-01.

rules.title: An earlier source change can move a later function
rules.symptom: A nearby edit changes another function without changing its semantics.
rules.construct: Compare cross-function effects after each source edit.
rules.explanation: Compiler numbering and phase context can couple functions in one TU.
rules.experiment: Record the strict status vector for the full TU, not one function.
rules.not_when: Do not attribute every peer change to source semantics.
rules.keywords: cross function coupling context

blupi_evidence.outcome: Across baseline, StopSound-only, and SB2-header full builds (9 TUs each), adding BOOL CSound::StopSound(int) changed accepted peers in button.cpp and menu.cpp; the StopSound-only candidate made all three STRICT baselines MISMATCH. SB1 confirmation incl. resolution by genuine declarations: see BLUPI-CTX-01.

rules.title: Probe placement can separate TU context hypotheses
rules.symptom: Top/end/before-function probes affect different later regions.
rules.construct: Compare the same count at three scratch-only insertion points.
rules.explanation: Different placement responses can reveal local versus delayed compiler work.
rules.experiment: Use small counts and compare all peer functions.
rules.not_when: No response in a bounded range does not disprove all context effects.
rules.keywords: count probe top end before function

blupi_evidence.tu: button.cpp; probes at top, before:MouseMove, and end
blupi_evidence.outcome: Counts 7-14 and 23-30 at top/before restore STRICT; no end placement from 0 through 32 does. Placement localizes the measured sensitivity to context preceding MouseMove, with phase attribution remaining an inference.

rules.title: A strict gain in one function can break a peer
rules.symptom: A source edit helps one function but shifts another.
rules.construct: Keep the full translation-unit strict result beside the target result.
rules.explanation: Shared TU context and data bindings couple otherwise separate bodies.
rules.experiment: Recompare every function after each successful edit.
rules.not_when: Do not promote a target-only gain without peer review.
rules.keywords: peer function strict status collateral

blupi_evidence.outcome: The 99-byte StopSound body at 0x23050 is STRICT (candidate object emits 112 bytes including 13 trailing NOPs); adding its declaration changes three accepted peer bodies from STRICT to MISMATCH in the StopSound-only full build.

rules.title: Automatic PCH mode is part of the build context
rules.symptom: A broad TU difference appears with /YX or include order.
rules.construct: Match the original IDE PCH settings and creation order.
rules.explanation: Automatic precompiled headers alter the compiler input stream.
rules.experiment: Compare with and without the authentic PCH procedure.
rules.not_when: Do not treat /YX as a generic speed flag.
rules.keywords: YX PCH translation unit

rules.title: Definition order can affect delayed compiler work
rules.symptom: Later functions shift after a definition or template moves.
rules.construct: Restore the evidenced definition order in the owning TU.
rules.explanation: Some VC5 work is deferred until later in the translation unit.
rules.experiment: Move only a real definition supported by source evidence.
rules.not_when: Do not add dummy definitions for alignment.
rules.keywords: definition order delayed template

rules.title: Commutative x87 order can be TU context
rules.symptom: Only the x87 operand load/reverse sequence differs.
rules.construct: Check TU context before swapping source operands.
rules.explanation: VC5 can choose x87 operand order from a numbered tie-break.
rules.experiment: Try a bounded scratch count probe before changing the expression.
rules.not_when: Keep noncommutative floating operations semantically fixed.
rules.keywords: x87 operand order context

rules.title: Test a flag on the target function, not by its name
rules.symptom: A flag change is proposed to explain a local instruction difference.
rules.construct: Change one compiler flag while holding source and context fixed.
rules.explanation: Option names do not predict which target body will improve.
rules.experiment: Compare the target and every peer under authentic settings.
rules.not_when: Do not globally promote a flag from one function.
rules.keywords: compiler flags target function

rules.title: Compiler package effects can vary by TU
rules.symptom: One function agrees across builds but a peer changes.
rules.construct: Sweep compiler builds on the owning TU with headers fixed.
rules.explanation: Front-end context and compiler package can interact.
rules.experiment: Compare per-function bytes and isolate compiler components before attribution.
rules.not_when: Do not call packages interchangeable from one helper.
rules.keywords: RTM SP2 SP3 compiler builds

rules.title: C++ unwind paths require the matching EH flag
rules.symptom: Cleanup calls or exception frames are missing.
rules.construct: Match /GX, then recover real C++ scopes and destructors.
rules.explanation: VC5 /GX enables the measured C++ unwind support.
rules.experiment: Compile a minimal throwing call with a destructor and inspect the object.
rules.not_when: Function-body bytes alone omit some EH sections.
rules.keywords: GX exception handling unwind

rules.title: Intrinsic calls can change with optimization mode
rules.symptom: memcpy/memset calls appear in one optimization mode but not another.
rules.construct: Use the source construct and authentic /O1 or /O2 setting.
rules.explanation: VC5 may call these intrinsics at /O1 and expand them at /O2.
rules.experiment: Compile both real flag sets and compare peer functions.
rules.not_when: Do not infer the source helper from the call alone.
rules.keywords: memcpy memset O1 O2 inline

rules.title: Constant, condition, and offset differences usually mean real source differences
rules.symptom: A value, branch condition, or memory displacement differs.
rules.construct: Check literal values, comparison operators, prototypes, and field layout.
rules.explanation: VC5 preserves many semantic differences rather than normalizing them.
rules.experiment: Trace the value or offset to source/header evidence before codegen experiments.
rules.not_when: Register-only and reorder-only diffs need a different first step.

evidence.counts: CurrentWrite STRICT at 0x14da0 (1,574 target bytes; 14 relocations) after a contiguous start-direction memcpy and signed int fwrite test; CurrentRead and FileExist cleanup variants remain mismatches.

rules.keywords: constant condition offset struct layout

blupi_evidence.outcome: Inherited int result accumulator plus else-if mismatched; private void declaration plus independent start/end checks emitted 128 COFF bytes and strictly matched the 115-byte target. The source changes were tested together.

rules.title: Many equivalent spellings produce identical code
rules.symptom: A syntax-only rewrite is proposed with no instruction evidence.
rules.construct: Avoid changing equivalent boolean, increment, or pointer spellings by default.
rules.explanation: VC5 normalizes many such forms; corpus perturbations were usually inert.
rules.experiment: Spend compiles on a source form that predicts a visible instruction change.
rules.not_when: A type, alias, or statement-boundary change is not merely spelling.
rules.keywords: inert equivalent spelling do not try

rules.title: Commuting arithmetic and expanding compound assignment are usually inert
rules.symptom: Only arithmetic operand order or compound-assignment spelling differs.
rules.construct: Do not try these as a byte-matching lever without evidence.
rules.explanation: Measured VC5 corpus perturbations rarely changed the output.
rules.experiment: Move to a different hypothesis after one inert check.
rules.not_when: This does not cover changed types or side effects.
rules.keywords: commute operands compound assignment negative

rules.title: Dummy declarations are not a source reconstruction
rules.symptom: Padding declarations are proposed to reach another code shape.
rules.construct: Use counter declarations only in scratch diagnostics.
rules.explanation: A probe response says nothing about whether the original contained padding.
rules.experiment: Remove probes before candidate source is promoted.
rules.not_when: Never use artificial code in canonical matching sources.
rules.keywords: dummy declaration padding artificial

rules.title: OutputDebug and empty UI destructors share a folded ret
rules.symptom: Many calls resolve to a one-byte ret at RVA 0x1f010.
rules.construct: Empty /Gy bodies in button.cpp, jauge.cpp, menu.cpp and misc.cpp are ICF candidates.
rules.explanation: The SB1 linker folds identical eligible code contributions. RVA 0x1f010 lies in the misc.cpp block; the former menu-destructor ownership claim was incorrect. The verifier reports FOLDED separately from STRICT.
rules.experiment: Compare object sections and call relocations, then verify the folded owner and RVA in the linked image.
rules.not_when: This is linker placement evidence, not a compiler-function match.

evidence.counts: 56 OutputDebug call sites; target RVA 0x1f010; five-TU comparison

rules.keywords: COMDAT folding FOLDED OutputDebug ret destructor linker

blupi_evidence.outcome: 56 calls resolve to the shared bare ret; physical oracle slot is misc.cpp, not menu.cpp

rules.title: LINK 5.10 ICF keeps the first equal contribution after unstable CRT qsort
rules.symptom: Identical bodies fold to a different object despite matching code and link order.
rules.construct: LINK 5.10.7303 /OPT:ICF with Windows MSVCRT qsort versus the VC5 runtime qsort.
rules.explanation: LINK appends eligible code-contribution records to the vector at 0x494398 (count 0x49439c), sorts them at 0x431fed by effective raw size and relocation count only (comparator 0x432130), then redirects later equivalent contributions onto the first at 0x432970. Equal-key order is CRT qsort-dependent; names and hashes are not sort tie-breakers. Dead candidates can affect the permutation before reference elimination.
rules.experiment: Trace the vector before/after qsort; predict its complete permutation with the actual CRT algorithm. Restore the historical runtime in a diagnostic tool session before changing source or object order.
rules.not_when: Historical qsort alone does not reproduce the current getter survivor. The oracle input vector remains unknown; arbitrary fillers, count tuning and unproved deletions are not fixes.

evidence.counts: 8 full-permutation checks: six 793-entry controls and two 790-entry dead-stub controls

Local CRT census: 12 DLL paths / six file hashes (MSVCRT20 2.11.000 product 2.10.000; MSVCRT40 4.10.6038; MSVCRT 5.00.7022, 5.00.7128, 5.00.7303, 6.00.8797.0), three byte-identical VC5 QSORT.C sources, and VC6 RTM LIBC qsort.obj. All use one middle-pivot/cutoff-8 algorithm with <=/>= scans and strict > shortsort. Six new serial LINK controls plus the pinned SP3 trace validate both complete 137-entry import permutations and the complete 793-entry ICF permutation; input keys/names/module order agree. Five DLLs bind all 111 CRT imports; MSVCRT20 lacks four exports and is a qsort-only control. Every output is byte-identical to baseline: IAT 15/128 oracle slots, USER32 2/35, frame filter before ehvecdtr. VC6 static qsort/shortsort/swap code corresponds to 6.00.8797.0 except five resolved call-relocation fields (not a strict object match). This excludes the inventoried CRT substitutions on these inputs; unobserved 4.20.x/6.00.8168 DLLs remain untested.

rules.keywords: LINK ICF COMDAT qsort MSVCRT survivor contribution order dead code ArrayUnwindFilter FrameUnwindFilter

blupi_evidence.outcome: Historical ICF qsort keeps ehvecdtr at 0x243c0 and entry 0x24d10 (oracle 0x243f0/0x24d40); host keeps frame at 0x27360 and entry 0x24cf0. Removing documented SB2 PlaceDecor8..10 has zero accepted regressions but does not solve survivor choices.

rules.title: RTM changes two SB1 sound helpers under fixed SP3 headers

rules.construct: Same sound TU, fixed headers, flags, oracle and link context; change compiler tree.
rules.explanation: SB1 evidence rejects universal VC5-build interchangeability. The RTM cause is not isolated to c1xx or c2.
rules.experiment: Compare both helpers and all TU peers; isolate compiler components before attribution.
rules.not_when: Do not infer that every RTM function differs.

rules.keywords: RTM SP3 sound compiler build

rules.title: __FILE__ and __LINE__ are observable SB1 inputs
rules.symptom: A path string or diagnostic line argument differs even when surrounding logic matches.
rules.construct: TRY_DS passes __FILE__ and __LINE__; VC5 embeds the source path and line values.
rules.explanation: The oracle contains F:\Profil\sound.cpp; a local absolute or relative source path emits a different literal. Line shifts can change diagnostic arguments.
rules.experiment: Keep source line numbering and compile path stable; inspect the data relocation and argument pushes.
rules.not_when: Do not mask string/data differences as codegen noise.

evidence.counts: F:\Profil\sound.cpp at RVA 0x7b484; TraceErrorDS strict at RVA 0x1ffa0

rules.title: Treat decompiler prototypes and merged control flow as hypotheses
rules.symptom: Pseudocode suggests a different prototype, merged branch, or guessed field name.
rules.construct: Translate instructions, call targets and field offsets into a minimal source candidate; compile and compare.
rules.explanation: The SB1 pilot found useful body/call structure but unreliable inferred parameters, return widths, and field names.
rules.experiment: Check prototypes from ret/stack behavior, then compile the smallest semantic source form and use strict cmpfunc verification.
rules.not_when: Pseudocode similarity is not evidence of source identity.

evidence.counts: 7 targeted compiles; 5/6 selected functions strict after translation and relocation proof; ChangeSprite remained mismatch

rules.keywords: decompiler Ghidra prototype calling convention field offset branch ChangeSprite

blupi_evidence.function: ChangeSprite; CEvent::FlushInput; CButton::TreatEvent; CMenu::TreatEvent; two wrappers
blupi_evidence.outcome: instruction-led translation resolved five selected cases; ChangeSprite still differs

rules.not_when: This is one SB1 function and one candidate form, not a general rule against local caching.

rules.title: Incomplete shared-header declarations shift VC5 TU context of including files
rules.symptom: Adding the real StopSound declaration changes MouseMove and other accepted functions in TUs that include sound.h.
rules.construct: Recover the authentic declaration set and order from SB1 evidence; compare all peers after each header change.
rules.explanation: Under the pinned SP3 build, MouseMove responds to pre-function count context in two bounded windows, while end-of-TU probes do not. A strict StopSound body therefore does not establish a safe header context.
rules.experiment: Compile all accepted functions with baseline and real-declaration-only scratch headers; use top/before/end probes diagnostically, then remove them.
rules.not_when: Never keep filler declarations to land in a probe window; the probe only shows that the original had a different preceding declaration count - find the real declarations (here: unreconstructed helper methods of the same class).

evidence.counts: 99 count-probe compiles; 27 full-TU builds across baseline, StopSound-only, and SB2-header contexts; 3 accepted peer regressions

Resolution: real SB1 declarations for the sound helpers (PlaySoundDS(int,int,int,int) 0x22f00, PlaySoundDS(int,int,int) 0x22fc0, PlayImage 0x230c0, Play 0x23220) make StopSound STRICT while CButton::TreatEvent, CButton::MouseMove and CMenu::TreatEvent stay STRICT (copied-tree all-TU build).

Second instance: six declarations gated per TU regressed CButton::MouseMove when unguarded; completing all SB1 class declarations (full method inventories in plausible order) made them unconditional with MouseMove still STRICT (317/318 accepted). Remaining GetBlupiInfo window +24..27/+32 top/before only -> missing preceding decblock bodies.

Authentic def.h removals reduce existing CButton::Create static symbol suffix by 443 (enum), 62 (14 operators), 12 (MAKE helpers), total 517. Four private whole-tree states have 3/3/5/4 accepted regressions; tables+44 restores GetBlupiInfo and adds STRICT DecorNextAction (272 bytes). 859 serial TU count-probe compiles measure peer windows, including new IsVentillo thresholds 106/150; no probes retained in candidate source.

DX5 authentic-header state at 70d630c: moving existing misc.h (31 predicted counter numbers) and dectables.h/obstacle.h (106) before decor.h restores MoveObjectSort STRICT at 0x13b20 (240 bytes, both relocations verified). Both relative header orders pass all active accepted entries; moving either header alone leaves MoveObjectSort MISMATCH. Seven serial whole-tree verify runs and one baseline fnprobe; supervisor gate (F: free) 113,344 bytes, zero regressions; integrated. No new declaration or function-body change. Exact historical include order remains a hypothesis.

rules.keywords: sound.h declaration count MouseMove StopSound peer regression

Pre-function probes restore MouseMove at counts 7-14 and 23-30; end probes do not through 32. No original header context is established. rules.title: Local arrays: function-scope arrays are laid out by ascending size; sibling-block arrays share one slot
rules.symptom: Stack displacements of local buffers differ (e.g. [esp+0x10c] vs [esp+0xa8]) although frame size matches.
rules.construct: Which scope each array is declared in, and which arrays live in disjoint sibling blocks.
rules.explanation: VC5 SP3 /O2 /GX (35 isolated probes): function-scope arrays are placed in ascending size order independent of declaration or first-use order; arrays declared in sibling blocks/cases share one slot sized to the largest; small (12/28-byte) arrays keep separate slots; passing an address or using a struct of equal size does not move a slot; a destructor in a throwing try adds a 4-byte slot.
rules.experiment: Map every target [esp+N] buffer to a source variable; group them into ascending runs; each run is one scope level (function scope first, then inner block groups); declare buffers accordingly and recompile.
rules.not_when: Scalar spills and register-allocated locals follow other rules; the rule is measured on VC5 SP3 /O2 only and inner-block group ordering is still a hypothesis.
rules.keywords: stack slot local array buffer layout ascending size scope block share frame

blupi_evidence.function: CEvent::ChangePhase (target map consistent with function-scope ascending run + inner block run)
blupi_evidence.outcome: Rule measured in micro TUs; application to ChangePhase pending

rules.title: A SIB base/index swap can be caused by the control-flow shape of another block in the same function
rules.symptom: Same effective address, SIB base and index registers swapped, early in a large function; equivalent address spellings do not change it.
rules.construct: Shape of other blocks in the same function (switch vs if-chain, block order), not the address expression itself.
rules.explanation: VC5 allocates registers function-wide; changing a later block's control-flow shape changed which register became base/index in an earlier loop. Wide TU count probes (end 0-64 step 1, 64-512 step 16; top/before 0-64) never flipped it, so it was not TU context here.
rules.experiment: After 2-4 genuine address spellings fail, rule out context with WIDE probes (end and top/before), then align other blocks of the same function to the target's shape (switch/if-chain, block order) and re-check the early SIB.
rules.not_when: Narrow count probes (e.g. 0-2) prove nothing; if a wide end probe flips it, treat it as back-end TU context instead.

evidence.counts: CEvent::TreatEventBase +0xAC SIB matched after the Escape handling took the target if-chain shape; identical prefix 172 -> 730 bytes; context probes negative over the ranges above

rules.keywords: sib base index swap register allocation function-wide switch if-chain shape

rules.title: SIB base/index order follows the identity of the index variable (shared vs separate locals)
rules.symptom: Same effective address, base and index commuted (e.g. 8a 54 0e 25 vs 8a 54 31 25); address spellings, context probes and compiler builds do not change it.
rules.construct: Whether two loops/blocks reuse ONE index local or use separate locals for the same role.
rules.explanation: VC5 SP3 /O2: the choice of base vs index register for [reg+reg+disp] followed which variable supplied the index; reusing a single player-index local (as the original did) reproduced the target order, separate locals commuted it. Lexical scope and the count of unused locals alone did not matter. Reproduced in a 112-byte micro TU.
rules.experiment: For each commuted SIB, identify the index variable; try merging same-role index locals into one (or splitting a shared one) and recompile; confirm in a micro TU when unsure.
rules.not_when: If wide context probes flip it, treat it as TU context; if a later block's control-flow shape flips it, see BLUPI-REG-01.

evidence.counts: CEvent::ChangeButtons 0x1b220 became STRICT (2,854 B, 83 relocations) after sharing one player-index local; 112-byte micro reproduction; TreatEventBase: 36 variants show index identity matters, scope/unused locals do not

rules.keywords: sib base index commuted shared local index variable identity loop

rules.title: Declaration-count sensitivity: c2 orders operands by keys that hash front-end symbol IDs
rules.symptom: A function's operand order, SIB base/index order or evaluation order flips when unrelated declarations are added or removed before it, in contiguous windows of probe counts with sharp edges.
rules.construct: Any commutative or paired-operand expression of equal cost whose operands contain symbols (locals, this, globals, functions) declared after a varying number of front-end entities.
rules.explanation: VC5 SP3 C1XX assigns each front-end entity the next value of the counter at C1XX VA 0x104ccb58; the IDs travel in the IL and c2 stores them at symbol +0x28. c2 keys every expression as (cost << 16) | H, where H (0x4053bf) XORs opcode constants, F(constant) and F(symbol ID) with F(s) = (s & 0xffff) ^ (s >> 16), and orders paired operands by unsigned descending key (0x408d58, merge sort 0x40922a/0x409306, swap path 0x4058dc). For two equal-cost operands only bit b = highest_set_bit(C_A ^ C_B) of the shared symbol contribution decides, giving windows of width 2^b and period 2^(b+1). A later pass may re-sort with different keys, so the emitted order can follow a later comparison than the first.
rules.experiment: Run tools/c2trace/ctxpredict.py on the function: it reports each context-sensitive comparison and the window around the current count. Then look for genuine declarations or include orders that move the decisive symbol ID into the good window.
rules.not_when: Residues insensitive to 0-300 probes (TreatEventBase, DrawButtons) are not key-order decisions; a change of expression topology or cost needs a new capture.

evidence.counts: 60/60 held-out predictions (MoveObjectSort 109-236/365-492, MockeryDetect 142-397 bad, IsDeepWater bit 0x40, IsVentillo bit 0x100, 2 micro TUs, 4 CButton suffixes)

rules.keywords: declaration count symbol id hash expression key operand order window include order context probes c1xx counter

rules.title: Front-end ID costs of declarations (SP3 /GX /O2), and local-static suffixes as a direct ID readout
rules.symptom: Estimating how many symbol IDs a header or declaration block contributes before a function.
rules.construct: extern/global/typedef, prototypes, enums, structs, guarded headers, unused locals, unused inline functions.
rules.explanation: Measured on fresh micros: extern/global/typedef 1; prototype without parameters 1, with two parameters (named or unnamed) 3; enum with three enumerators 4; empty or two-field struct 7; opening an empty guarded header 1; unused local 1; unused inline int f(){return 0;} 2, with one parameter 3. The Blood II approximation (named parameters only, inline shell 4-5) is not general. A function-local static's COFF suffix (e.g. CButton::Create ttypes$S34693) is its front-end ID, so it reads the counter directly in any object.
rules.experiment: Read a local static's $S suffix in the candidate object to measure the counter before and after a header change, instead of counting declarations by hand.
rules.not_when: Costs of complex templates, classes with members and C++ special members were not measured.

evidence.counts: 15 registered cost predictions (12 hit before calibration); suffix arithmetic 443/62/12 predicted 4/4

rules.keywords: declaration cost counter prototype parameter enum struct inline local static suffix front-end id

rules.title: Force one expression-key comparison to classify a residue as key-order or not
rules.symptom: A residue whose cause is unknown: declaration-count effect, allocator decision or source form.
rules.construct: Any open function; the diagnostic forces each 0x408d58 comparison near the residue and compares the forced object with the oracle.
rules.explanation: tools/c2trace/keyforce.py (ported from blood2_recon's keys/force method) lists every comparator 0x408d58 call while a function is compiled, with keys, symbol IDs and domains, and can override one result inside the c2 child. If a single reversal removes the residue, the residue is a key-order decision and the required symbol-ID or temp-number relation follows from the hash (BLUPI-CTX-03); if all residue-local reversals are byte-inert, look at allocation or lifetimes (BLUPI-ALLOC-*) instead. SB1 results: TreatEventBase 53 reversals keep all 8 bytes; ChangePhase 64 residue-local reversals inert; Build gains only collateral and would need impossible shifts (about 31,600 IDs); DrawButtons comparison #1310 needs F(line2) < F(text) and moving the genuine line2 declaration reproduces it but worsens the function (63 -> 755 bytes).
rules.experiment: keyforce.py capture NAME src/X.cpp; keyforce.py list/trace NAME FUNC; keyforce.py force NAME FUNC EVENT RESULT. Judge by aligned instructions as well as raw bytes: a lower raw count can hide a worse aligned result.
rules.not_when: Forced objects are diagnostics, never source. Combinations of forced comparisons were sampled only sparingly.

evidence.counts: 283 sequential forces over 4 functions; 1 genuine source test

rules.keywords: force comparator key order diagnostic classify residue declaration temp allocator

rules.title: Statements consume front-end symbol IDs too: an earlier function's spelling shifts every later function's IDs
rules.symptom: A key-order residue (BLUPI-CTX-03) in a later function changes when an earlier function in the same TU is respelled, even though the earlier function's bytes stay identical.
rules.construct: Control-flow and expression constructs in any function compiled earlier in the TU.
rules.explanation: Measured on VC5 SP3 /O2 /GX with a function-local static's $S suffix (the front-end ID, BLUPI-CTX-04) after one function body: if 1, if/else 2, && 1, || 2, while 3, for 3, switch 4 plus 1 per case, goto+label 2, cast 1, local 1, ternary 0. So the counter is not only declarations: equivalent spellings of earlier code (if/else vs ternary, || chains, casts, labels) are authentic levers that shift the IDs deciding later operand orders. The phenomenon was first documented for VC4 by homm1-decomp (see scratch/research/techniques.md for the source); this rule records the VC5 SP3 measurement.
rules.experiment: Measure the counter before and after with a local static's $S suffix or tools/c2trace/ctxpredict.py; compare against the window the predictor reports.
rules.not_when: Residues that are not key-order decisions (BLUPI-CTX-05 force diagnostic inert) do not respond to ID shifts.
rules.keywords: statement cost symbol id counter if else switch case label cast loop earlier function spelling

rules.title: Struct temporaries vs scalar call arguments change VC5 scratch-register choice
rules.symptom: Identical instruction shapes; the oracle rotates scratch registers (eax, ecx, edx, eax...) where the candidate reuses eax for every temporary, including in code unrelated to the calls.
rules.construct: A callee taking POINT (built per call by a helper/temporary) versus the same callee taking two ints (x, y).
rules.explanation: VC5 SP3 /O2: AdaptBorder calls AdaptMidBorder five times. With MAKE_POINT(...) struct temporaries every argument temporary is eax; with AdaptMidBorder(int x, int y) the same pushes rotate eax/ecx/edx/eax and the later m_decor index calculation follows (eax, ecx, edx). Bytes pushed are identical, and the callee body is byte-identical under either signature; only its mangled name differs, which a relocation hides. Passing an existing POINT variable is neutral; the inline helper's form (initializer, member stores, derived-class constructor) does not matter. Reproduced in a 30-line micro TU.
rules.experiment: When a register-only residue rotates in the oracle but not the candidate, look for calls whose struct-by-value arguments are built per call (POINT(...)/RECT(...)); try a scalar-parameter signature for the callee (check the callee body stays strict, then rename its accepted record).
rules.not_when: If the callee's own code reads the struct as a unit (e.g. copies it), the scalar signature changes code. TreatEventBase's residues did not respond (its POINT arguments are existing variables).

evidence.counts: micro TU 7 variants; AdaptBorder STRICT, AdaptMidBorder still STRICT

SB1 negative: DrawMap local RECT aggregates, shared block, member assignments and clip reuse retain a 0x38 frame and 159 differing non-relocation bytes; all-four-before-Build restores frame 0x28 but still differs by 146 bytes. Build existing-pos reuse changes 8 bytes; separate zero aggregates retain its body. These diagnostics are not strict matches.

rules.keywords: point struct temporary by value scalar arguments signature register rotation make_point

blupi_evidence.outcome: STRICT after AdaptMidBorder(int x, int y)

rules.title: A shared error block at the end of the source is laid out inline after the last check
rules.symptom: Oracle has the cleanup (free/fclose; return FALSE) right after the last validity check and jumps over it with je; the candidate tests the inverse (jne) and places the cleanup at the end.
rules.construct: `if (bad) goto error; ... success code ... return TRUE; error: cleanup; return FALSE;` (Planet Blupi decio style) versus `if (ok) goto success; error: cleanup; success: ...`.
rules.explanation: VC5 SP3 /O2 lays out the end-of-source error block directly after the last conditional goto (with jump threading into it from earlier NULL checks); the reconstruction's goto-success arrangement makes it move the block to the end instead. FileExist and CurrentRead became byte-identical with the Planet Blupi form.
rules.experiment: When a cleanup block is displaced, restore the ancestor's goto-error structure with the error label at the end of the function.
rules.not_when: Functions whose oracle really has the block at the end.
rules.keywords: goto error cleanup block layout success label fopen fread free fclose

rules.title: An uninitialized local can read the dead parameter slot
rules.symptom: Oracle loads a value from a parameter's stack slot ([esp+N]) on a path where the candidate copies an initialized local or the cached parameter register.
rules.construct: Local left uninitialized on some path (original bug) versus an explicit default assignment.
rules.explanation: ChangeSprite: SB1 never assigns hCursor when no sprite matches. VC5 placed hCursor in the dead parameter slot of `sprite` (cached in edi), so the else path reads [esp+0xc]. `hCursor = (HCURSOR)sprite;` produced `mov eax, edi`.
rules.experiment: If the oracle reads a parameter slot where the source has a default assignment, try removing the assignment (the original may have relied on undefined behaviour).
rules.not_when: When the read value is used in a way that would be observably wrong.
rules.keywords: uninitialized local parameter slot reuse bug changesprite hcursor

rules.title: TreatEventBase register residues do not respond to code-neutral source, context, toolchain or flags
rules.symptom: Two coupled free-choice sites (toggle edx/ecx, PostMessage hwnd edx) choose the first free register in the candidate and the next one in the oracle; all other 6,608 code bytes and 62 jump-table entries match.
rules.construct: (none - negative result)
rules.explanation: About 150 single-TU probes, all with identical code elsewhere: local declaration order (13), shared case-label order, switch case source order, code-identical copies, dead stores, local types, local renames (12), blank lines, extern-declaration count probes 0-32 before the function, stubbing all 96 preceding function bodies, scalar signatures for its POINT callees, all seven VC5 compiler trees, and 25 code-generation flags (an earlier sweep was invalid: Git Bash had rewritten '/X' flags into paths; redone with MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1). Reduced examples show the choice is function-global (code added after the sites can flip it, period 3 in inserted loads), so the original must differ in something code-producing elsewhere or in an untested invisible property.
rules.experiment: Do not repeat these families. Next candidates: argument/expression forms that leave bytes identical but change temporaries (see BLUPI-REG-03).
rules.not_when: Other functions where a code-neutral form did flip registers (BLUPI-REG-01/02/03).
rules.keywords: treateventbase register rotation negative flags toolchain context probes declaration order

rules.title: Free scratch-register choices follow allocations emitted earlier in layout order
rules.symptom: A free scratch-register choice changes when code is added elsewhere in the function, including in a different switch case, without any change near the site.
rules.construct: Allocations in blocks emitted (laid out) before the residue site: code before it in the function, and switch case bodies that the dispatch places ahead of it.
rules.explanation: VC5 SP3 /O2. Micro TU: an extra scratch load in case 0x102/0x150 (emitted before the case 0x100 body) flips the 0x100 case's free choices whether the case is written first or last in the source; in case 0xA0/0x50 (emitted after) it never does. In TreatEventBase the same load flips the residues when placed in WM_NCMOUSEMOVE (dispatch emits it before WM_KEYDOWN) and not in WM_CHAR, WM_KEYUP, WM_MOUSEMOVE, WM_LBUTTONUP or WM_PHASE_DEMO (emitted after). Case value and source position as such do not decide; emission order does. A first write-up that said 'descending case value' was wrong and is corrected here.
rules.experiment: For a register-only residue, look for differences in code emitted before the site (including out-of-line case bodies placed ahead of it), not in later source lines.
rules.not_when: Residues outside switch statements; the rule says which code can influence the choice, not how to find the original difference.
rules.keywords: switch case order value register allocation rotation descending

blupi_evidence.outcome: rule established; TreatEventBase residue still open

rules.title: Expression temporaries rotate eax/ecx/edx; plain-copy register locals take the first free register
rules.symptom: Identical code except scratch registers; the oracle's choice is one or two steps further along eax -> ecx -> edx than the candidate's at a free-choice site.
rules.construct: Whether a loaded value is an expression temporary (`V1(h[k])`, `h[a] = h[b] + 1`) or a named local that is a plain copy of a load (`t = h[k]; V1(t);`).
rules.explanation: VC5 SP3 /O2 micro TUs (build/tmp/ra): serialized loads separated by calls get eax, ecx, edx, eax... - a per-function rotor carried across calls and blocks in emission order (BLUPI-REG-04). Every free temporary takes the rotor's next register and advances it; forced registers (call results, cdq/idiv, shift counts) do not advance it; `a + b` advances it twice. A local that is a plain copy of a load is allocated to the first free register (eax) and does not advance the rotor. Both forms emit identical bytes whenever the rotor points at the first free register, but leave the rotor in different states, which changes later free choices.
rules.experiment: Count the rotor steps needed (oracle vs candidate at the first differing free site, mod 3). In code emitted before that site, look for single-use loads that could be plain-copy locals in the original (or the reverse) and convert one; verify bytes before the site stay identical.
rules.not_when: Locals used more than once may be promoted to callee-saved registers instead; computed locals (`t = x + 1`) behave as temporaries.
rules.keywords: register rotor round robin eax ecx edx temporary local copy first free allocation

rules.title: c2.exe temp assignment: preference, then rotor (0x491120), then first free; rotor reset per function
rules.symptom: Scratch-register differences (eax/ecx/edx) in otherwise identical code; inserting or removing an unrelated load shifts choices with period 3.
rules.construct: Number and kind of compiler temps (tuple-defined values) allocated before the site, in block (layout) order.
rules.explanation: c2.exe SP3 0x435c37 gives each temp defined by a tuple a register: a recorded preference (copy from/to a register-holding value; set by the pass at 0x42ac33) if free and non-interfering; otherwise, when the flag at 0x48fb60 is set, the first free non-interfering register at or after the rotor pointer 0x491120 over the list eax, ecx, edx, after which the pointer moves to the slot after the chosen one; otherwise first free from eax. Only this rotor path moves the pointer (hardware watchpoint). The pointer resets to eax per function (0x42a90e). Loads folded into compares never pass through it.
rules.experiment: tools/c2trace: `capture`, `assigns NAME SYMBOL` (path/register per temp), then `shift NAME SYMBOL RVA`; a MATCH at assignment K means the original had one rotor step more/less just before K; `map` locates K in the code. In-memory rotor shifts are diagnostics, never source.
rules.not_when: Values held in callee-saved registers (global colouring, color.c), compare-only loads (BLUPI-REG-07) and forced registers (call results, idiv, shift counts) are outside this mechanism.
rules.keywords: rotor round robin temp register assignment preference c2 0x435c37 0x491120 eax ecx edx

blupi_evidence.outcome: residue located to one rotor step between assignments 20 and 21

rules.title: Compare-only loads use a per-block scratch rotor (0x4911a8): first non-live register from the last pick
rules.symptom: `mov r,[mem]; cmp/test r` differs only in r; the load is the first of its basic block and the oracle has eax while the candidate skips to ecx/edx (or the reverse).
rules.construct: Which values are live in IR order at the compare: a constant or value assigned by an earlier statement keeps its register busy; evaluation order inside the statement matters.
rules.explanation: c2.exe SP3 0x42b2c4 picks code-generation scratch registers: index of the last pick at 0x4911a8 (reset to n-1 at every basic block, so a block starts at eax), list of n=8 registers at 0x491100. Pass 1 takes only registers already used in the function (descriptor flag 0x10), pass 2 any; live registers are skipped, byte operations exclude registers above ebx. It never touches the temp rotor.
rules.experiment: Identify the block's earlier scratch picks; check which register is live at the compare in IR order (statement order, not schedule). Move the assignment that holds the register (e.g. a repeated `pos.x = 330;`) to before the block and re-probe.
rules.not_when: Loads that are real temps (used by more than the compare) follow BLUPI-REG-06.
rules.keywords: scratch register compare-only load per block rotor 0x42b2c4 0x4911a8 live set code generation

blupi_evidence.outcome: predicted and fixed the +0x19c6/+0x19ce register regions by moving pos.x = 330 before strchr

rules.title: Preference pass: a temp copied into a register-holding value prefers that register
rules.symptom: A setcc/toggle result lands in the rotor's register in one context but in a specific register in another (e.g. `m = !m; b = m;`).
rules.construct: What the temp is copied into: a callee-saved local (b) or an intermediate value already in a scratch register.
rules.explanation: c2.exe SP3 0x42ac33 (store at 0x42b051) sets lr+0x2c to the register descriptor of the destination of a copy; 0x435c37 takes it if free and non-interfering, without moving the rotor. If the preferred register is busy (e.g. the callee-saved local is live), the rotor decides.
rules.experiment: c2trace `assigns`: path 'pref' and the pref column show it; the micro copy build/c2/cheatlab.py reproduces the TreatEventBase toggle.
rules.not_when: Preferences for esp are never recorded; preferences only cover registers 1-8.
rules.keywords: preference coalescing copy register descriptor 0x42ac33 0x42b051 toggle setcc

rules.title: Pooled zero constant: memory zero stores and compares interned before colouring, kept only at positive score
rules.symptom: Ours hoists `xor reg,reg` and uses it for `mov [m],reg` stores and `cmp [m],reg` tests across several blocks; the oracle stores immediate 0 and tests with `mov reg,[m]; test reg,reg`.
rules.construct: Several `m_x = 0` / `= FALSE` member stores and `if (m_y)` member tests in one region of a function.
rules.explanation: VC5 SP3 c2 interns eligible memory zero operands as a class-13 virtual constant before colouring (pool scan 0x414a64, eligibility 0x4156b6, intern 0x417fb7). The cost pass 0x40ee1d scores the surviving range: each zero store +1, each materialisation -1, zero compares 0.
